reasons: Summary accurately reflects source claims about max-weight algorithm, throughput optimality, slotted-time operation, differential backlog computation, topology-dependent rate selection, and known limitations (delays, interference challenges).

Mechanisms correctly capture differential backlog computation (commodity selection via max positive difference, arbitrary tie-breaking) and topology-dependent rate selection (observing state, choosing rate matrix from feasible set).

Unknowns properly identify gaps: exact tie-breaking procedure, handling of probabilistic errors/failures in basic algorithm, feasibility under interference, and delay trade-offs — all consistent with source's mentions of arbitrary tie-breaking, extended formulations for errors, implementation difficulties, and large delays.
No unsupported mechanisms or invented execution details; all claims trace to source text.
Qualifiers like 'may introduce large delays' and 'difficult to implement exactly' are preserved from source.
